items.title: Driven By Global Growth, Live Nation Posts $10.1B In Q3 Revenue
items.summary: Live Nation Entertainment reported third-quarter revenue of $10.1 billion, up 19% year on year, as 61 million fans attended its concerts. CEO Michael Rapino said ticket sales through October reached 170 million, already ahead of all of last year, with nearly 180 million fans expected for 2026. Year to date, international markets surpassed the U.S. in both concert attendance and sponsorship revenue, and international markets drove 60% of fan growth and a majority of sponsorship revenue. Concerts revenue was $8.7 billion (up 20%), Ticketmaster $870 million (up 9%) and sponsorship $506 million (up 14%).
items.what_it_means: Live music's growth is being led outside the U.S., and brands are following the same international crowds.

items.title: Can MLS Capitalize on Son-Mania?
items.summary: Front Office Sports reports that Son Heung-min's LAFC away matches have drawn crowds in Tottenham and South Korea shirts, including at Citi Field for NYCFC. D.C. United worked with the DC Spurs supporters group on a group package that put more than 900 fans into Audi Field, and a post-event survey found more than half would attend another D.C. United match. Clubs are bundling Son games with other fixtures and reaching Korean community groups to try to turn one-off visitors into partial plans and season tickets. Son himself told FOS he still sees Spurs shirts with his name at away matches across the country.
items.what_it_means: A visiting star can fill seats with someone else's fans; the commercial test is whether clubs convert that night into ongoing membership.

items.title: Texas Tech details escalating payments in Galaxy stadium naming-rights deal
items.summary: Citing the Lubbock Avalanche-Journal, SBJ reports that Texas Tech's 15-year naming-rights deal with Galaxy Digital for Galaxy Stadium starts at $4 million in 2026-27 and rises 3% a year to more than $6 million by 2040-41, for a total of about $74.4 million. Fees are paid in two equal instalments each year, and Galaxy can opt out on 30 June 2036. The deal guarantees at least six home games a year and lets Galaxy put up to $100,000 of each year's fee toward Tech athletes' NIL.
items.what_it_means: A college stadium naming deal is bundling escalating cash with a built-in NIL spend and a mid-term exit option for the sponsor.

items.title: World Triathlon partnership boosts Hyrox's Olympic ambitions
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports that Hyrox's partnership with World Triathlon makes the hybrid racing format a recognised discipline inside an Olympic sport's governing body. World Triathlon's president said the deal should help national federations grow participation and reach new audiences. The partnership removes a major barrier to Olympic entry, though it is too late for Los Angeles 2028 and any push would aim at Brisbane 2032. It is still unclear whether Hybrid Racing would enter as a new sport or as a discipline under triathlon.
items.what_it_means: A participation-led fitness brand is buying Olympic pathway credibility by nesting inside an existing federation rather than waiting for a new sport slot.

items.title: VEON to Acquire Interest in Jungo TV and All Women's Sports Network (AWSN) to Accelerate Digital Entertainment Growth
items.summary: VEON announced it will take a 33.75% equity stake, with control rights, in JungoTV Holdco, the holding company of Los Angeles-based Jungo TV. Jungo TV's portfolio includes the All Women's Sports Network (AWSN), a 24/7 women's sports channel co-founded with Whoopi Goldberg, and is distributed in more than 60 countries via platforms such as Amazon Prime Video, Pluto TV, DIRECTV, Sling, Jio, SuperSport and MBC. VEON plans to expand that programming across its markets in Pakistan, Bangladesh, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan and Ukraine, targeting growth through subscriptions, advertising, sponsorship and content licensing. Jungo TV and AWSN will stay headquartered in Los Angeles under existing management.
items.what_it_means: A global telco is buying distribution for women's sports content into markets where it already owns the customer relationship.

items.title: Nostalgic Anaheim Ducks Hometown Remix jersey sparks surge in sales
items.summary: Citing The Athletic, SBJ reports that the Anaheim Ducks' Hometown Remix jersey, a modern nod to Mighty Ducks movie colours, sold out on Fanatics and was the only one of the 32 Remix sweaters to do so as of Wednesday night. Team SVP and CMO Merit Tully said the club sold more than 2,000 jerseys at its team store in the first 24 hours, the most in a single day since 1993, and more than 4,000 jerseys and related items over three days. The Ducks will wear the jersey in 10 games, and Tully expects another sales lift when they do.
items.what_it_means: Nostalgia tied to a team's entertainment origin story can outsell a league-wide jersey drop when the design feels like the club's own.

items.title: In TikTok first, Raiders pregame live show draws plenty of eyeballs
items.summary: SBJ reports that before their Oct. 25 home game against the Rams, the Las Vegas Raiders ran a 49-minute pregame show on TikTok Live and counted 220,000 unique views, a format TikTok says is new among NFL teams. Rather than studio Xs and Os, the club hired TikTok personality Lycette Beatty to broadcast from inside Allegiant Stadium as fans arrived, with interviews and a focus on the Vegas spectacle. Senior director of content strategy Gavin Rivera said the goal was reach on a platform with a wide, diverse audience, and that the result exceeded expectations.
items.what_it_means: A team pregame show on TikTok can out-reach traditional studio content when it sells the night out, not the playbook.

items.title: Disney continues sports content push abroad as the Rich Eisen Show is added to select EMEA markets
items.summary: SBJ reports that The Rich Eisen Show is expanding for the first time onto ESPN on Disney+ in selected Europe, Middle East and Africa markets, including the UK, Ireland, South Africa, the Netherlands and Nordic countries. The move sits inside a wider Disney push to grow ESPN on Disney+ internationally, with the service set to carry ESPN's Super Bowl stream in more than 55 international markets in February. Disney+ also recently licensed Formula E coverage into more than 100 countries and territories.
items.what_it_means: Disney is packing talk, live sport and niche series onto the same international streaming shelf rather than treating overseas ESPN as rights-only.

items.title: As '26 season concludes, O'Donnell says NASCAR has encouraging momentum
items.summary: In his first state-of-the-sport press conference as NASCAR CEO, Steve O'Donnell said attendance across 38 race weekends was up 5% overall and up 12% for kids under 12, with social impressions up 34% despite posting less. He said interest among 18-34 fans is at its highest since 2013, while TV viewership remains strong but still a focus. Stellantis plans to bring Dodge back to the Cup Series in 2027, giving NASCAR four manufacturers at the top level for the first time in well over a decade.
items.what_it_means: NASCAR is measuring success in who shows up at the track and who comes back younger, not only in the broadcast number.

items.title: Sky Sports acquires WTGL rights
items.summary: Sky Sports has secured exclusive UK rights to the WTGL, the new women's team golf league in partnership with the LPGA, for the 2026 and 2027 seasons, alongside a further two years of the men's TGL presented by SoFi. The inaugural WTGL season begins on 8 November and will use the same mic'd-up, risk-reward team formats as the men's competition, with players including Charley Hull, Lottie Woad and Jeeno Thitikul. Sky framed the deal as part of its commitment to women's sport and to bringing fans closer to major golf moments.
items.what_it_means: A UK broadcaster is pairing a new women's team golf product with its existing men's indoor league rather than treating it as a one-off special.
